the N-terminal region (NTD) of Munc13 is the center of a protein interaction network that includes Aczonin/PIC, Bassoon, Rim, and CAST.

the molecular architecture of the active zone and the mechanisms of its assembly and function.
the molecular organization of the presynaptic active zone.
the molecular mechanisms of neurotransmitter release at the presynaptic active zone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aczonin and Rim1 interact with each other, and with Munc13 and Bassoon.
the active zone is a highly complex and dynamic structure, which is composed of many protein components.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found a protein interaction node in the active zone of synapses that centers on the Munc13- and Rim-binding domains of Bassoon, the Munc13-binding domains of Aczonin, and a region of CAST that binds to both Bassoon and Aczonin.
the active zone proteins Aczonin, CAST1, Bassoon, Munc13-2, Rim1 and Munc13-3 form a protein network that is centered on the N-terminal domain of Munc13.
we show that Aczonn, Bassoon, Munc13- 1, CAST1/ELK, and Rim are multiply interconnected and we provide evidence that the Aczonn coiled-coil domains are involved in the assembly of the active zone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a protein interaction node at the release site is a central organizing feature of the active zone.
the protein machinery of the active zone is tightly interconnected and that Aczonin and its coiled-coil domains play important roles in synaptic assembly and function.

Aczonin/PIC and Bassoon, two scaffolding proteins that have been implicated in the assembly of the active zone and the control of synaptic transmission, form a complex with the active zone protein Rim1.
